summary.title: Language-agnosticism #39: is_dynamic_language + is_special_method facts
summary.what: Added two Grammar facts (base neutral False): is_dynamic_language() -> bool and is_special_method(name) -> bool. python overrides both (dynamic; __x__ dunder rule); javascript/typescript/ruby override the dynamic flag. Removed the hardcoded _DYNAMIC_LANGUAGES = {python,javascript,ruby} set and the __x__ dunder checks from shared structural compute: orphans._confidence and relational._meaningful now take the grammar and delegate. Added test_dispatch_semantics.py. Suite 206->210.
summary.why: The dynamic-dispatch confidence penalty and the special-method discount were Python-shaped hardcodes buried in shared metric code -- the same overfit class as #34/#36/#37. The __x__ check treated any __init__-named symbol as special regardless of language (wrong for a Go func named __init__), and the dynamic set scored TS orphans as more certain than the JS they compile to.
summary.user_goal: Language-agnosticism #39: is_dynamic_language() + is_special_method() grammar facts replacing the hardcoded _DYNAMIC_LANGUAGES set and __x__ dunder checks in shared orphans/relational compute

decisions.point: Name the special-method fact is_dunder (per the work-list) or something language-neutral
decisions.rationale: 'dunder' is the Python token (__x__), not the cross-language concept (a name invoked implicitly by the runtime). A Go/Rust grammar implementing is_dunder() would be incoherent. Same concept-over-token call as renaming #37's noise fact.
rejected: is_dunder(name) -- bakes Python's naming convention into the contract

decisions.point: Whether TypeScript counts as a dynamic language (the legacy set was {python, javascript, ruby})
decisions.rationale: TS erases to JS at runtime; string-keyed access, `any`, dynamic import and reflect-metadata defeat static reference counting exactly as in JS. Scoring a TS orphan as more certain than the JS it compiles to would be incoherent. A deliberate extension beyond the legacy oracle, documented in-code.
rejected: Matching the legacy set exactly (python/js/ruby) -- preserves the oracle but treats TS orphans as more certain than JS, which is indefensible

decisions.point: is_special_method for non-Python languages (Ruby operator methods, Java toString, etc.)
decisions.chose: Base default False; only Python overrides (the __x__ rule)
decisions.rationale: Only Python has a crisp name-pattern convention for implicit dispatch. orphans only inspects top-level functions/classes (not methods), so other languages' implicitly-invoked methods (initialize/toString) are structurally out of scope there; relational's marginal __send__-style cases are not worth a fuzzy per-language special-name set. Preserves Python behavior exactly; for non-Python a literal __x__ symbol is now correctly treated as ordinary.
rejected: Enumerating Ruby/Java/C# special-method names (fuzzy, scope creep, low value)
Keeping the __x__ check as a shared default (re-introduces the Python convention into shared code)

rejected.reason: runts is Python-by-construction -- it parses Python line syntax (docstrings, imports, dunder assignments) and only runs on __init__.py modules (package_init_name() is None elsewhere). Not shared-code overfit.
